Growth stocks are attractive to many investors, as above-average financial growth helps these stocks easily grab the market's attention and produce exceptional returns. But finding a growth stock that can live up to its true potential can be a tough task.

By their very nature, these stocks carry above-average risk and volatility. Moreover, if a company's growth story is over or nearing its end, betting on it could lead to significant loss.

However, the task of finding cutting-edge growth stocks is made easy with the help of the Zacks Growth Style Score (part of the Zacks Style Scores system), which looks beyond the traditional growth attributes to analyze a company's real growth prospects.

Our proprietary system currently recommends Palantir Technologies Inc. (PLTR) as one such stock. This company not only has a favorable Growth Score, but also carries a top Zacks Rank.

Studies have shown that stocks with the best growth features consistently outperform the market. And for stocks that have a combination of a Growth Score of A or B and a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) or 2 (Buy), returns are even better.

While there are numerous reasons why the stock of this company is a great growth pick right now, we have highlighted three of the most important factors below:

Earnings Growth

Earnings growth is arguably the most important factor, as stocks exhibiting exceptionally surging profit levels tend to attract the attention of most investors. And for growth investors, double-digit earnings growth is definitely preferable, and often an indication of strong prospects (and stock price gains) for the company under consideration.

While the historical EPS growth rate for Palantir Technologies is 42.5%, investors should actually focus on the projected growth. The company's EPS is expected to grow 118.2% this year, crushing the industry average, which calls for EPS growth of 26.7%.

Cash Flow Growth

While cash is the lifeblood of any business, higher-than-average cash flow growth is more important and beneficial for growth-oriented companies than for mature companies. That's because, growth in cash flow enables these companies to expand their businesses without depending on expensive outside funds.

Right now, year-over-year cash flow growth for Palantir Technologies is 665.2%, which is higher than many of its peers. In fact, the rate compares to the industry average of 9%.

While investors should actually consider the current cash flow growth, it's worth taking a look at the historical rate too for putting the current reading into proper perspective. The company's annualized cash flow growth rate has been 50.9% over the past 3-5 years versus the industry average of 18.1%.

title: PLTR vs. ACN: Which Leading Tech Stock Should You Consider?
detail:
PLTR vs. ACN: Which Leading Tech Stock Should You Consider?
Shuvra Shankar Dey
Mon, October 26, 2026 at 12:47 PM EDT 5 min read
ACN
PLTR
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Both are major players in the enterprise technology and AI space, with Palantir Technologies PLTR focusing on advanced data and AI-driven software platforms and Accenture plc ACN operating as a global IT services and consulting powerhouse deeply involved in digital transformation and AI deployments.

While Palantir specializes in developing cutting-edge platforms such as Foundry, Gotham, and AIP to empower organizations with data-driven intelligence and decision-making capabilities, Accenture integrates AI across industries through its consulting expertise, cloud capabilities, and vast client network. Together, they represent two complementary forces in the AI ecosystem, one providing transformative technology and the other driving large-scale adoption.

The Case for PLTR

One of Palantir's most important competitive advantages is its Ontology framework. Rather than treating enterprise information as disconnected data points, the platform models an organization around the real-world assets, customers, orders, facilities and operational relationships that define its business.

This structure allows applications to act on enterprise information within established rules, permissions and workflows. As a result, Palantir is positioned to become more than an analytics vendor. Its software can operate as a digital foundation connecting data, decisions and business processes.

The investment case becomes particularly compelling as artificial intelligence adoption expands. More capable AI models alone do not guarantee meaningful business outcomes. Enterprises still need systems that connect models with trusted data, workflows and controlled actions. Palantir's Artificial Intelligence Platform, or AIP, addresses this gap by helping organizations deploy AI within operational environments rather than keeping it confined to experimental applications.

Once a customer builds its initial use case around Palantir's platform, additional applications can be created on the same underlying structure. This potentially improves returns on the original implementation while increasing the difficulty and cost of replacing the platform.

Another potential catalyst lies in Palantir's deployment model. Historically, the company has relied heavily on highly skilled engineers to work closely with customers during implementation. That approach can accelerate value creation but may also limit how quickly Palantir can onboard new customers.

Greater automation and self-service capabilities could therefore represent an important next phase of growth. If PLTR can reduce the level of manual engineering required for new deployments while maintaining implementation quality, it could accelerate customer additions without needing a comparable expansion in sales or technical headcount. Such operating leverage would further strengthen an already attractive business model.

title: Brokers Suggest Investing in Palantir Technologies (PLTR): Read This Before Placing a Bet

Investors often turn to recommendations made by Wall Street analysts before making a Buy, Sell, or Hold decision about a stock. While media reports about rating changes by these brokerage-firm employed (or sell-side) analysts often affect a stock's price, do they really matter?

Let's take a look at what these Wall Street heavyweights have to say about Palantir Technologies Inc. (PLTR) before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage.

Palantir Technologies currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.71, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 31 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.71 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy.

Of the 31 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 21 are Strong Buy and one is Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 67.7% and 3.2% of all recommendations.

Brokerage Recommendation Trends for PLTR
Broker Rating Breakdown Chart for PLTR

Check price target & stock forecast for Palantir Technologies here>>>

The ABR suggests buying Palantir Technologies, but making an investment decision solely on the basis of this information might not be a good idea. According to several studies, brokerage recommendations have little to no success guiding investors to choose stocks with the most potential for price appreciation.

Are you wondering why? The vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover often results in a strong positive bias of their analysts in rating it. Our research shows that for every "Strong Sell" recommendation, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations.

This means that the interests of these institutions are not always aligned with those of retail investors, giving little insight into the direction of a stock's future price movement. It would therefore be best to use this information to validate your own analysis or a tool that has proven to be highly effective at predicting stock price movements.

Zacks Rank, our proprietary stock rating tool with an impressive externally audited track record, categorizes stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), and is an effective indicator of a stock's price performance in the near future. Therefore, using the ABR to validate the Zacks Rank could be an efficient way of making a profitable investment decision.

ABR Should Not Be Confused With Zacks Rank

Although both Zacks Rank and ABR are displayed in a range of 1--5, they are different measures altogether.

title: How Low Can Snowflake Stock Go?

How Low Can Snowflake Stock Go?
Trefis Team

Snowflake (SNOW) stock returned 131.9% over the six months to October 23, 2026, outpacing the 7.0% return for the S&P 500. The stock closed that day 11.8% below its October 9 high, leaving a holder still with a large gain to protect if the market turns. Snowflake has traded only since September 2020. That leaves just five market shocks to learn from. So how low could Snowflake stock go if the market sells off, and how long could it stay down?

How Far Has Snowflake Stock Fallen In Market Shocks?

Snowflake has fallen more than twice as far as the broader market. Across the five shocks, the stock dropped 30.8% on average, compared with 13.4% for the S&P 500. Its worst fall in these shocks came during the 2022 inflation shock and Fed tightening, when Snowflake lost 66% while the index lost 24%. In the most recent one, the 2025 US tariff shock, the stock fell 30.0% against 19.0% for the index.

Recoveries have usually taken months rather than years. The median time from Snowflake's low to its earlier high was 2.3 months. The 2022 fall is the exception. The stock needed 49.9 months to bounce back from its June 2022 low, and only returned to its January 2022 high on August 10, 2026.

Snowflake Grows Faster But Still Loses Money

Snowflake is bigger and growing faster than a year ago. Revenue over the twelve months to July 31, 2026 was $5.4 billion, up 32.0%, against growth of 28.4% in the twelve months before. Management said on the September 2 call that the latest quarter benefited from its core data platform business and a meaningful step up in AI revenue.

The company still loses money, but less of it. Its operating loss was 22.8% of revenue over the latest twelve months, down from 37.4% a year earlier. The business also brings in cash. Free cash flow reached $1.19 billion, up from $734 million a year earlier. Debt, though, has grown. Snowflake owed $2.76 billion on July 31, 2026, against $313 million two years earlier.

What Is Getting Harder For Snowflake Now?

Snowflake has moved to borrow a lot more money. On September 28, 2026, the company announced a sale of convertible notes that pay no interest, due in 2029 and 2031. A day later it priced the sale at an upsized $3.75 billion. That is more than the $2.76 billion of debt Snowflake owed at the end of July.

Profit on each sale is also under pressure as AI work grows. Management lowered its fiscal 2027 forecast for product gross margin, its own adjusted measure, on September 2, 2026. The forecast fell to 74% from 75% three months earlier. Management said the revised outlook includes a higher revenue mix from fast-growing AI workloads, which have a lower contribution margin today. Snowflake is expected to report its fiscal Q3 2027 results in December 2026. Its product gross margin is the figure to watch in that report.

title: I Said Palantir Stock Would Top $220 This Year. Here's What It Has to Prove on Nov. 2.
detail:

NVDA

Back in August, I made a bullish prediction about Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ: PLTR): I said the artificial intelligence (AI) software company would reach $220 per share before the end of 2026, driven by its outstanding revenue growth and increasing demand from commercial customers.

I'm sticking with that prediction. But Palantir has some work to do.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

On Friday, shares were trading in the $190 to $198 range, leaving the stock roughly 11% to 16% below my target. And with Palantir scheduled to report third-quarter earnings on Nov. 2, investors are about to get a much better idea of whether my prediction will come true.

I think Palantir needs to deliver three things to make a run at $220.

Image source: Getty Images.
1. Quarterly revenue needs to top $2.3 billion

Palantir has established a remarkable track record of accelerating revenue growth, thanks largely to businesses adopting its Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP).

Second-quarter revenue jumped 93% year over year to $1.94 billion. U.S. commercial revenue was particularly impressive, climbing 149% to $764 million, while U.S. government revenue increased 90% to $809 million. Those are outstanding numbers for a company of Palantir's size.

But management's third-quarter revenue guidance of approximately $2.16 billion implies sequential growth of roughly 12%, compared with about 19% in the second quarter. That seems awfully conservative to me.

Palantir has consistently beaten its revenue guidance this year, and another quarter of 19% sequential growth would put revenue at approximately $2.3 billion.

That's the number I'm watching. If Palantir's revenue is growing at an accelerating rate, that would be an important bullish signal to the market.

2. Sales tied to the company's AI sovereignty efforts must increase

One of Palantir's more interesting opportunities involves the market for AI sovereignty services -- helping organizations maintain control over their data and AI operations rather than surrendering much of that control to external technology providers. It has been a primary focus of CEO Alex Karp in recent months.

It's a natural fit for Palantir. The company's software already helps customers connect their data, build digital models of their operations, and deploy AI applications while maintaining control over sensitive information.
